articles.title: Rochdale's Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield to Receive £20m for Community Improvements
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale council is set to accept nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising the historically overlooked areas of Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield, with plans to improve local facilities and services.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale's Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield are set to benefit from nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising these historically overlooked areas. The Rochdale council is expected to accept the Pride in Place funding at a town hall meeting scheduled for August 25, 2026. This funding amounts to £19.6 million over the next decade, equating to just under £2 million annually.

The funding aims to address various local issues, including tackling congestion, improving parking, creating new green spaces, enhancing local facilities, and expanding maternity services. However, as of now, no specific plans have been established for how the money will be allocated. The council will form a Neighbourhood Board, comprising local community figures and officials, to develop a proposal for the funding's use.

The Neighbourhood Board will include Rochdale MP Paul Waugh and Coun Daniel Meredith, the council’s regeneration lead, and will be chaired by Laura Rodwell of the M6 Theatre group. They have until November 30, 2026, to submit a four-year plan to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, which is necessary to unlock the funding. An initial £150,000 has already been granted to establish the board and generate the plan.

Local residents have expressed skepticism about the funding, citing years of neglect and lack of investment in their communities. Ken Whittle, a long-time resident, voiced concerns about the area's decline, while others have called for better healthcare services and community facilities. The upcoming Neighbourhood Board will aim to incorporate local views into the future plans, with consultation events already held by MP Paul Waugh.
